Description: On: AMP shows who's online, and its kick and ban buttons and 'last player leaves' tasks work. Build 42 no longer prints joins and leaves to the console, so without this AMP always shows 0 players. This starts the server with the game's detailed log, which also prints player IP addresses and RCON passwords. AMP's console hides both, but the game's own server-console.txt file still has them, so only give file access to people you trust. The detailed log adds some extra lines to the console too.

DisplayName: Hide Steam IDs in AMP's console
Description: On: players' Steam account numbers show as [hidden] in AMP's console, like their IP addresses. The game's own log files still have them. Turn this off if you need to see which Steam account a player used.

The message everyone in game sees when the server finds a Workshop mod update. The server only checks when it's told to: in AMP, open Schedule and add a task that sends the console command checkModsNeedUpdate every 10 or 15 minutes. Players who already have the new version can't join until the server restarts, so restart when it suits you. Leave this empty to send no message.
DefaultValue: A mod has been updated. The server will restart soon to install it.

Description: Required. The password for your in-game admin account (the username below), not the one players use to join. The game resets the admin account to this password every time the server starts. Use a password you don't use anywhere else: anyone you give access to this server in AMP may be able to see it. Every box on these pages saves when you click away from it and takes effect after a restart. Change server settings in these boxes, not in the game's .ini file, because AMP rewrites that file from them every time the server starts.

The name of your in-game admin account. The game creates it on the first start. If your game is started in debug mode, only admin accounts can join: others see 'Debug connection is not allowed for non admin.'

The name the game uses for this server's settings files and world. Changing this starts a brand new world with fresh settings files. The old world stays on disk under its old name. Use letters, numbers, dashes or underscores only.

The most memory (RAM) the server can use. It starts at 3072 MB (3 GB). The game's own dedicated server files give two figures: 3 GB in ProjectZomboid64.json, and 16 GB in StartServer64.bat on Windows. For Build 42 we recommend at least 10240 MB (10 GB), adjusted for the mods you run. The game's memory manager grows towards this limit whether it needs the memory or not, so leave enough for Windows and anything else running on the machine. If the console shows OutOfMemoryError, raise this.

Decides who wins when a sandbox setting (zombies, loot, world and so on) is changed both here and in the game's admin menu. Last change wins: when the server starts, only the boxes you've changed here since the last start are applied, so changes made in game are kept. AMP always wins: every sandbox box is applied each time the server starts, so changes made in game only last until a restart. Mod sandbox settings are never touched, whichever you pick. To make these boxes match what the game is really using, after changes in game or after bringing in a world: start the server once, then in the File Manager right click Zomboid/Server/servertest_SandboxImport.ini (your save name in place of servertest) and choose Import Configuration. A world you bring in is safe: on its first start here, nothing from AMP is applied to it until you import or change a box. Presets and mod settings: use the game's own settings editor. On your PC, open Project Zomboid, click HOST, then Manage settings, then Create New Settings or Edit Selected Settings. Give it the same name as this server's save name. Choose the same mods as this server, use Apply Preset if you want one, change anything you like, and save. It's saved in the Zomboid\Server folder in your user folder. Stop this server, upload only the saved servertest_SandboxVars.lua to Zomboid/Server in the File Manager, replacing the old one, then start and import as above. Leave the .ini it also saves, because AMP's own boxes set those settings. With AMP always wins, AMP's boxes replace the uploaded sandbox settings.
ZGC is what the game's own launcher uses on Windows 10 and later, and G1GC is what it uses on older Windows. ZGC grows towards the memory limit even when it doesn't need the memory.
Added to the Java part of the start command. Leave this empty unless a guide tells you what to add.
Added to the end of the start command, for example -ip 192.168.1.10 to use one network address. Leave this empty unless you need it.

RCON lets other programs, like a Discord bot or an admin tool, send commands to the server using the RCON password (set in Start here). When this is on, only programs on this server machine can use RCON, so nothing on your network or the internet can reach it. Turn it off only if a program on another machine needs RCON, and keep the RCON port closed on your router.

Build 42 is the game's normal Steam version. Unstable gets test builds first, and players must be on the same version as the server to join. After changing this, stop the server, click Update, then start it. Build 41 worlds don't load in Build 42. Don't put mods in AMP's own Steam Workshop box on this page, because it causes a Steam login loop. Add mods in Configuration, Server, Mods and map.

On: anyone can join, and their account is made the first time they log in with a password. Off: only people already on the whitelist (or allowed Steam IDs) can join. The Indie Stone's Build 42 multiplayer notes suggest a whitelisted server, so off. In the settings file: Open.
The message shown in chat right after a player logs in. Use <LINE> for a new line and <RGB:1,0,0> for colour. In the settings file: ServerWelcomeMessage.
DefaultValue: Welcome to Project Zomboid Multiplayer! <LINE> <LINE> To interact with the Chat panel: press Tab, T, or Enter. <LINE> <LINE> The Tab key will change the target stream of the message. <LINE> <LINE> Global Streams: /all <LINE> Local Streams: /say, /yell <LINE> Special Steams: /whisper, /safehouse, /faction. <LINE> <LINE> Press the Up arrow to cycle through your message history. Click the Gear icon to customize chat. <LINE> <LINE> Happy surviving!

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: On: while the server is dropping network packets, new logins are refused with 'Server is too busy.' The game only checks this on a server hosted from inside the game with Steam on, so it has no effect on a dedicated server. In the settings file: DenyLoginOnOverloadedServer.

How many players can be on at once. When it's full, new joiners are refused with 'ServerFull', or wait in the queue if 'Login queue' is on. The Indie Stone's Build 42 notes suggest 20 players or fewer. In the settings file: MaxPlayers.

Players whose ping stays above this, in milliseconds, are kicked, and players above it when they join are turned away. 0 turns this off. While playing, each ping over 1000 counts as 1000, so a value of 1000 or more never kicks anyone already in. Staff with the right permission are never kicked for lag. In the settings file: PingLimit.

On: when a character dies, the player's account is taken off the whitelist. On a closed server ('Open to anyone' off) they can't come back without an admin. In the settings file: DropOffWhiteListAfterDeath.
A password everyone must type to join. Leave empty for no password. A /reloadoptions applies a new password without a restart. In the settings file: Password.
How many different accounts one Steam user can create here. 0 means no limit. Only checked when the server runs in Steam mode. In the settings file: MaxAccountsPerUser.
On: a player can bring extra split-screen players on the same PC. Off: only the first player on each PC can join. In the settings file: AllowCoop.
On: players joining a busy or full server wait in a queue instead of being refused. Staff with priority login skip ahead. In the settings file: LoginQueueEnabled.
Seconds a queued player gets to finish connecting when it's their turn, before the next person is let in. In the settings file: LoginQueueConnectTimeout.
On: usernames can use letters outside basic English, for example Cyrillic. Checked when an account logs in. In the settings file: AllowNonAsciiUsername.
Set from the ports AMP gives this instance.
Set from the ports AMP gives this instance.
On: the server is listed in the in-game public server browser. In the settings file: Public.

The server name shown in the in-game browser and the Steam browser. The game sets 64 characters as the limit for this but doesn't enforce it when the server starts, so keep it to 64 or fewer. In the settings file: PublicName.

The description shown in the in-game public server browser. The game sets 256 characters as the limit for this but doesn't enforce it when the server starts, so keep it to 256 or fewer. In the settings file: PublicDescription.
On: the player list shows Steam names and avatars. In the settings file: SteamScoreboard.
On: Steam's VAC anti-cheat is switched on for this server. A -steamvac value on the command line overrides this. In the settings file: SteamVAC.
On: the server asks your router to open its ports automatically when it starts. If the server hangs while starting, switch this off. In the settings file: UPnP.

Forces the IP address the server sends to the in-game public server list. Left empty, the server uses the address the list site reports back to it. The game asks for an IPv4 address here when that reported address looks like IPv6. In the settings file: server_browser_announced_ip.
On: account names show above players' heads. In the settings file: DisplayUserName.
On: the character's first and last name show above their head. In the settings file: ShowFirstAndLastName.
On: a player whose face is covered shows a 'disguised' name instead of their own. In the settings file: UsernameDisguises.

On: disguised players show no name at all instead of the 'disguised' label. This switches disguises on by itself, even with 'Face coverings disguise names' off. In the settings file: HideDisguisedUserName.
Forces every new character to start at these x,y,z map coordinates. 0,0,0 means use the normal spawn choices. In the settings file: SpawnPoint.
Items every new character starts with, as item types separated by commas, for example Base.Axe,Base.Bag_BigHikingBag. In the settings file: SpawnItems.
On: fire is disabled in multiplayer, except campfires. In the settings file: NoFire.
On: players can smash world objects and walls with a sledgehammer. In the settings file: AllowDestructionBySledgehammer.
On: players who aren't admins can only sledgehammer things inside their own safehouse. Needs 'Sledgehammer destruction' on. In the settings file: SledgehammerOnlyInSafehouse.
On: players can sleep in beds and cars, and when everyone online is asleep, time speeds up. Usually off on public servers. In the settings file: SleepAllowed.
On: characters get tired and must sleep. Only works when 'Sleeping allowed' is also on. In the settings file: SleepNeeded.
On: players can be knocked down. The game marks this as work in progress that may cause position desync. In the settings file: KnockedDownAllowed.

On: sneaking players can stay hidden from other players. Each watcher's game rolls a chance to spot them based on distance, light, cover and their Sneaking level, but anyone within 2 tiles, or sprinting, is always seen. Off: sneaking doesn't hide anyone. In the settings file: SneakModeHideFromOtherPlayers.

On: while time runs very fast, for example while everyone sleeps, the game adjusts how quickly animals get hungry and thirsty and makes them wander less often. In the settings file: UltraSpeedDoesnotAffectToAnimals.
On: a player who dies can respawn at the spot where they died. In the settings file: PlayerRespawnWithSelf.
On: a player who dies can respawn next to a split-screen partner on the same PC. In the settings file: PlayerRespawnWithOther.

How fast time runs while everyone online is asleep, which needs 'Sleeping allowed'. It's measured against a 30 minute day whatever 'Day length' is set to, so 40 passes a day in about 45 real seconds, and zombies break doors and barricades faster by the same amount. In the settings file: FastForwardMultiplier.

The most items one container can hold, counting every small item such as each nail and everything inside bags. 0 means no limit. What players carry isn't limited, and an empty container takes anything, even a full bag. In the settings file: ItemNumbersLimitPerContainer.
On: dead players' bodies are also removed when the corpse removal timer in the sandbox settings clears bodies. In the settings file: RemovePlayerCorpsesOnCorpseRemoval.
On: players get a 'delete all' button on bins. In the settings file: TrashDeleteAll.
On: you only see another player's name when you point your mouse at them. In the settings file: MouseOverToSeeDisplayName.
On: other players behind your character are hidden, the same way zombies you can't see are hidden. In the settings file: HidePlayersBehindYou.
On: players running into each other bump, and the one running can trip and fall. Sprinting into someone always ends in a fall. In the settings file: PlayerBumpPlayer.

Which other players appear on the in-game map: 1 nobody, 2 faction and safehouse mates, 3 those plus players you can see, 4 everyone. Staff who can see the world map always see everyone. In the settings file: MapRemotePlayerVisibility.
On: players see their map coordinates in the lower right corner. In the settings file: ShowCoordinates.

On: any player can claim one building as a safehouse once they've survived the days you set, even if 'Admins only safehouses' is also on. If both are off, nobody can claim a safehouse. In the settings file: PlayerSafehouse.

On, with 'Players can claim safehouses' off: only admins and moderators get the option to claim safehouses, and they can hold more than one. If 'Players can claim safehouses' is also on, this makes no difference and anyone can claim. In the settings file: AdminSafehouse.
On: people who aren't members can walk into a safehouse. Off: only members can. The game spells this setting Trepass. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowTrepass.
On: fire can damage safehouses. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowFire.
On: people who aren't members can take items from a safehouse. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowLoot.
On: a player who dies can respawn inside a safehouse they belong to, once they've ticked the respawn box in that safehouse's window. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowRespawn.

DisplayName: Days survived to claim a safehouse
Description: In-game days a character must survive before they can claim a safehouse. 0 means straight away. In the settings file: SafehouseDaySurvivedToClaim.
Real-world hours a safehouse can go unvisited before it's removed. 0 turns removal off. In the settings file: SafeHouseRemovalTime.
On: players can also claim shops and other buildings that aren't homes. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowNonResidential.
On: name disguises don't work inside safehouses. In the settings file: SafehouseDisableDisguises.
The largest area a safezone claim can cover, as width times height in tiles. 0 means no limit. In the settings file: MaxSafezoneSize.
On: safehouse wars can happen, and during a war safehouse protection is lifted. In the settings file: War.
Seconds of warning before a war begins. In the settings file: WarStartDelay.
How long a war lasts, in seconds. In the settings file: WarDuration.

Only matters when 'Safehouse wars' is on. Each war declared on a safehouse that the owner refuses or doesn't answer in time counts once, and when the count reaches this number the safehouse is released. Wars that are accepted and fought don't count, and 0 means it's never released this way. In the settings file: WarSafehouseHitPoints.

DisplayName: Protection only while owner is offline
Description: On: a safehouse acts like a normal house while its owner or any member is online, so its protection only applies while they're all offline. In the settings file: DisableSafehouseWhenOwnerConnected.
On: players can create factions. In the settings file: Faction.

DisplayName: Days survived to make a faction
Description: In-game days a character must survive before creating a faction. 0 means straight away. In the settings file: FactionDaySurvivedToCreate.

DisplayName: Members needed for a faction tag
Description: How many members a faction needs before its owner can set a name tag. In the settings file: FactionPlayersRequiredForTag.
On: players can hurt and kill each other. Usually off, or on with 'PvP safety switch' so players can switch their own PvP on and off. In the settings file: PVP.
On: PvP events are reported in admin chat. In the settings file: PVPLogToolChat.
On: PvP events are written to the server log files. In the settings file: PVPLogToolFile.

Only matters when PvP is on. On: each player chooses whether they're open to PvP, and a hit is only blocked when both players have it switched off, so a player who has it on can also hurt players who have it off. Off: everyone can hurt everyone. In the settings file: SafetySystem.
On: a skull shows over players who have PvP switched on. In the settings file: ShowSafety.

Turning PvP on is instant. Turning it back off keeps the player open to PvP for this many real seconds first, and the switch can't be used again until then. 0 makes it instant. In the settings file: SafetyToggleTimer.

Real seconds added to a player's cooldown each time they attack another player while open to PvP, stacking with each attack. They can't change their PvP switch until it runs out. 0 adds none. In the settings file: SafetyCooldownTimer.

Only matters when 'PvP' and the 'PvP safety switch' are on. If a player leaves while their switch is changing or their attack cooldown is running, their character stays in the world for twice this many seconds, longer if they're hit, and their quit buttons stay greyed out until the cooldown ends. 0 turns this off. In the settings file: SafetyDisconnectDelay.

DisplayName: Hit back straight away in PvP
Description: On: a player who has just been hit by another player can swing back straight away. In the settings file: PVPMeleeWhileHitReaction.

Multiplies melee damage when one player hits another. It's a straight multiplier, not a percentage, so 1 leaves damage unchanged and the default 30 is 30 times that. In the settings file: PVPMeleeDamageModifier.

Multiplies ranged weapon damage when one player shoots another. It's a straight multiplier, not a percentage, so 1 leaves damage unchanged and the default 50 is 50 times that. In the settings file: PVPFirearmDamageModifier.
On: the global /all chat channel is available. In the settings file: GlobalChat.

Which chat channels exist, as short codes separated by commas: s say, r radio, a admin, w whisper, y yell, sh safehouse, f faction, all global (only if 'Global chat' is on). In the settings file: ChatStreams.
On: a message goes to everyone in chat whenever a player dies. In the settings file: AnnounceDeath.
On: a message goes to everyone in chat when a player kills an animal. In the settings file: AnnounceAnimalDeath.
On: built-in voice chat is available. In the settings file: VoiceEnable.
Within this many tiles, other players' voice chat plays at full volume. Further out it fades smoothly to silence at 'Voice hearing range'. In the settings file: VoiceMinDistance.

Beyond this many tiles, voice chat is silent, and between 'Voice full volume range' and this it fades smoothly. Voice heard through a radio uses the radio's own range instead. In the settings file: VoiceMaxDistance.
On: voice chat sounds come from the speaker's direction. In the settings file: Voice3D.
On: players with the admin, GM or moderator role can't send chat messages out over in-game radios. Overseers aren't covered. In the settings file: DisableRadioStaff.
On: admins can't send chat messages out over in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioAdmin.
On: GMs can't send chat messages out over in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioGM.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: Meant to stop overseers sending chat messages over in-game radios, but the game only checks it for admins, GMs and moderators, so this has no effect. In the settings file: DisableRadioOverseer.
On: moderators can't send chat messages out over in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioModerator.
On: invisible staff can't transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioInvisible.
Path to a text file of banned words, one per line, for the chat filter. The file is read once at start, so edits take effect after a restart. In the settings file: BadWordListFile.

Path to a text file of allowed words, one per line. The chat filter won't block these even if they contain a banned word. The file is read once at start, so edits take effect after a restart. In the settings file: GoodWordListFile.
What happens to someone who uses a banned word: they're banned, kicked, or the violation is just recorded. Their message is still sent, with the word replaced. In the settings file: BadWordPolicy.
The text that replaces a banned word in chat, up to 16 characters. In the settings file: BadWordReplacement.
The longest chat message a player can type, in characters. In the settings file: ChatMessageCharacterLimit.
How many seconds a player must wait between chat messages. In the settings file: ChatMessageSlowModeTime.
On: the server's built-in Discord bot connects and relays chat. Read when the server starts, so changes take effect after a restart. In the settings file: DiscordEnable.
The access token for the Discord bot the server logs in as. Keep this secret; the game leaves it out of the public option list. In the settings file: DiscordToken.
The Discord channel name (not the ID) for relaying chat. The bot uses the first text channel with this name. In the settings file: DiscordChatChannel.
The Discord channel name (not the ID) where the bot posts log messages. In the settings file: DiscordLogChannel.

The Discord channel name (not the ID) where the bot listens for commands. Anything posted there runs as a server command with admin rights, so only let people you trust post in that channel. In the settings file: DiscordCommandChannel.

A web address the server posts short messages to: players joining and leaving, anti-cheat reports, and the server opening or closing. It works with a Discord webhook, no bot needed: in Discord, open the channel's settings, then Integrations, Webhooks, New Webhook, Copy Webhook URL. Paste it here and add /slack to the end.
Set from the ports AMP gives this instance.

Required. RCON lets other programs, like a Discord bot or an admin tool, send commands to the server using this password. Use a long password you don't use anywhere else: anyone you give access to this server in AMP may be able to see it, and the game keeps it in plain text in its settings file. By default only programs on this server machine can use RCON: see 'RCON from this machine only' in Remote admin (RCON).

The mod IDs to load, separated by semicolons, for example ModA;ModB. Each mod also needs its Workshop item number in Workshop Items, or nothing loads. One Workshop item can hold several mod IDs, so list each one you want. A backslash before an ID (\ModA) is optional, because the game removes backslashes before reading this list.
The map folders to load, separated by semicolons. Map mods go first and Muldraugh, KY goes last, for example MapModA;Muldraugh, KY. This can't be empty.
On: players whose game or mod files don't match the server's are refused. In the settings file: DoLuaChecksum.

The Steam Workshop item numbers, separated by semicolons with no spaces. Each number is at the end of the mod's Workshop page address, after id=. The game downloads these itself when the server starts. Don't use AMP's own Steam Workshop box on the Updates page.
Saves the loaded parts of the map every this many real minutes. 0 means only the normal saving, when areas unload. In the settings file: SaveWorldEveryMinutes.

How many backups the server keeps of each kind: at startup, after a game version change, and on the backup timer. Each kind keeps its own set, so you can have up to three times this number, and when a set is full the oldest one is deleted. In the settings file: BackupsCount.
On: a backup is made every time the server starts. In the settings file: BackupsOnStart.
On: a backup is made at start when the game version is different from the last run. In the settings file: BackupsOnVersionChange.
Makes a backup every this many real minutes while the server's running. 0 turns timed backups off. In the settings file: BackupsPeriod.

The world generation seed. The game only uses this when the world's generation data doesn't exist yet. Its tooltip says to delete map_worldgen.bin in the save to change it. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: Seed.
On: game time stops while nobody's online. In the settings file: PauseEmpty.

On: with more than one player online, control of each zombie passes to the next connected player every 2 seconds, in turn. Off: each zombie is run by the player grabbing or chasing it, or else the nearest player. In the settings file: SwitchZombiesOwnershipEachUpdate.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: The game uses the sandbox setting with the same name instead of this one. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: BloodSplatLifespanDays.

Multiplies how far a running car's noise reaches zombies, on top of 'Engine loudness to zombies'. Lower values make the noise pulse more often over a smaller area, and it never drops below a radius of 8, so 0 doesn't make cars silent. In the settings file: CarEngineAttractionModifier.
How often, in seconds, the server gathers multiplayer statistics. 0 turns statistics off. In the settings file: MultiplayerStatisticsPeriod.

The most packets of any one kind a player's game sends each second. Past the limit their game skips the extra packets, while the server only notes it in its debug log and doesn't kick anyone. In the settings file: MaxPacketsPerSecond.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: The game doesn't use this in 42.21. Ragdolls are switched off on every multiplayer server and client before this is checked. In the settings file: UsePhysicsHitReaction.
On: everyone hears thunder when staff ban or kick a player who's online. Automatic bans and kicks by the anti-cheat or the banned word filter don't play it. In the settings file: BanKickGlobalSound.
What the server does when it catches someone breaking the PvP safety rules: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). In the settings file: AntiCheatSafety.
What the server does when a player or vehicle moves faster than allowed: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). In the settings file: AntiCheatSpeed.
What the server does when a player walks through walls: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). This is Disabled by default. In the settings file: AntiCheatNoClip.
What the server does about impossible hits (damage, distance, weapon and vehicle hits): ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). In the settings file: AntiCheatHit.
What the server does about broken or unexpected network messages: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). This is Disabled by default. In the settings file: AntiCheatPacketException.
What the server does when someone uses powers their role doesn't have: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). In the settings file: AntiCheatPermission.
What the server does about impossible skill XP gains: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). The allowed amount follows the XP multiplier settings. In the settings file: AntiCheatXP.
What the server does about invalid safehouse actions (by owners, members or non-members): ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). In the settings file: AntiCheatSafeHouse.
What the server does about invalid player data or targets: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). In the settings file: AntiCheatPlayer.

What the server does when a player's game files still don't match the server's 60 seconds after the file check: ban, kick, log only, or nothing (Disabled). It only applies while the file check setting is on. In the settings file: AntiCheatChecksum.
On: the player list hides other players from each player. In the settings file: DisableScoreboard.
On: staff whose role allows hiding are left out of the player list. In the settings file: HideAdminsInPlayerList.
Which client commands are left out of (minus) or kept in (plus) the cmd.txt log. Write rules like -vehicle.* and +vehicle.fixPart, separated by semicolons. In the settings file: ClientCommandFilter.
Which player actions are written to the client action log, as action names separated by semicolons. In the settings file: ClientActionLogs.
On: skill level changes are written to the PerkLog log. In the settings file: PerkLogs.
The top speed for cars in multiplayer, in km/h. The speed anti-cheat uses the same number for vehicles. In the settings file: SpeedLimit.
On: players can't tow cars with cars in multiplayer. In the settings file: DisableVehicleTowing.
On: players can't tow trailers in multiplayer. In the settings file: DisableTrailerTowing.
On: players can't tow burnt-out wrecks in multiplayer. In the settings file: DisableBurntTowing.
Off: no cars spawn in newly explored areas. In the settings file: EnableVehicles.
How many cars spawn in newly explored areas. In the settings file: CarSpawnRate.

Multiplies how loud every vehicle engine is to zombies. 1 is normal and 0 is quietest. Vehicles pick up a change when they next load or have a part changed, and 'Car noise range for zombies' multiplies on top of this on a server. In the settings file: ZombieAttractionMultiplier.

On: cars are unlocked and don't need keys to start. Newly found cars also come with a full tank, a full battery, a top quality engine and a key in the glove box, and engines never fail to start in the cold. In the settings file: VehicleEasyUse.
How full the tanks of found cars are, for cars that have any fuel at all. In 42.21 Full gives the same amounts as Normal. In the settings file: InitialGas.
How often found cars are locked. In the settings file: LockedCar.
Multiplies how fast cars burn fuel. In the settings file: CarGasConsumption.
The general state of found cars' parts. In the settings file: CarGeneralCondition.
How much damage cars take in crashes. In the settings file: CarDamageOnImpact.

DisplayName: Damage from being hit by a car
Description: How much damage a player takes when hit by a car. When another player is driving, the PvP settings also decide whether the hit hurts. In the settings file: DamageToPlayerFromHitByACar.
On: traffic jams of wrecked cars appear in the places the map marks for them. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: TrafficJam.
How often found cars have a working alarm. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: CarAlarm.
On: people inside a car can be hurt when it crashes. In the settings file: PlayerDamageFromCrash.
In-game hours before a wailing car siren switches itself off. 0 means it doesn't switch off on its own. In the settings file: SirenShutoffHours.
The chance a found car has any fuel at all. In the settings file: ChanceHasGas.
How often you find well kept cars that a survivor looked after. In the settings file: RecentlySurvivorVehicles.
On: zombies head towards car sirens. In the settings file: SirenEffectsZombies.

The overall zombie amount. In the game's own settings screens, picking this also sets 'Population multiplier', but here they're separate boxes, so set both. The game also uses this directly for how many zombies are inside buildings and how dense the map is. None turns zombies off. Normal is the usual choice. In the settings file: Zombies.
Urban Focused uses the map's own zombie density for each area, so density varies from place to place. Uniform gives every area the same density. In the settings file: Distribution.

On: random patches across the whole map have their zombie density set to zero as the map loads, so zombies are spread less evenly. Off: the map's own zombie density is used everywhere. In the settings file: ZombieVoronoiNoise.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: A shortcut in the game's own settings screens: picking this fills in 'Zombie respawn (hours)', 'Unseen time before respawn' and 'Zombie respawn share'. Here, set those three directly. None or Low is a common pick. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: ZombieRespawn.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: A shortcut in the game's own settings screens: ticking this sets 'Zombie migration (hours)' to 12, and unticking sets 0. Here, set 'Zombie migration (hours)' directly. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: ZombieMigrate.

The actual size of the zombie population the game uses. The game's settings screens use these values: Insane 2.5, Very High 1.6, High 1.2, Normal 0.65, Low 0.15, None 0. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.PopulationMultiplier.
Multiplies the zombie population on day one. After that it grows towards the peak (see 'Peak multiplier' and 'Peak day'). In the settings file: ZombieConfig.PopulationStartMultiplier.
Multiplies the zombie population on its peak day. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.PopulationPeakMultiplier.
The in-game day the zombie population reaches its peak. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.PopulationPeakDay.
How many in-game hours between zombie respawns into cleared areas. 0 means zombies don't respawn. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RespawnHours.
How many in-game hours an area has to go unseen by players before zombies can respawn there. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RespawnUnseenHours.
What share of an area's population comes back each respawn, from 0 to 1. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RespawnMultiplier.
In-game hours between zombies drifting into empty areas, as the game describes it. The game says 0 stops migration. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RedistributeHours.
How far zombies try to walk towards the last sound they heard, as the game describes it. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.FollowSoundDistance.
How many zombies like to gather into one wandering group. 0 or 1 turns grouping off. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RallyGroupSize.
How much group size varies, as a percentage. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RallyGroupSizeVariance.
How far, in tiles, zombies walk to join a group. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RallyTravelDistance.
How far apart, in tiles, separate zombie groups stay. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RallyGroupSeparation.
How close, in tiles, group members stay to their group's leader. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.RallyGroupRadius.

How many zombies the server keeps in sync with each player before it starts deleting the extras to save performance. Only zombies that are outdoors, not chasing anyone and well away from that player are deleted. 0 means none are deleted. In the settings file: ZombieConfig.ZombiesCountBeforeDelete.

How fast zombies move. Random mixes speeds using 'Zombie sprinter percentage'. A zombie's speed is picked each time it's loaded into the world, and choosing Sprinters also makes zombies that are already loaded run. Casual groups often pick Shamblers or Fast Shamblers; players report sprinters can desync in multiplayer. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Speed.

When 'Zombie speed' is on Random, the percentage of zombies that sprint. The rest are shamblers or fast shamblers. Ignored for the other 'Zombie speed' choices. In the settings file: ZombieLore.SprinterPercentage.

How hard zombies hit doors, windows, barricades and cars. It also sets how many zombies it takes to drag a character down (2 on Superhuman, 6 on Weak, 3 otherwise) and how easily a character fends off an attack. The damage a zombie's attack does to a character stays the same. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Strength.
How hard zombies are to kill. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Toughness.

How the infection spreads. Blood and Saliva: bites always infect, and scratches and lacerations can too. Saliva Only: only bites infect. Everyone's Infected: wounds infect as usual, and everyone who dies comes back as a zombie, whatever killed them. None: wounds don't infect and nobody comes back. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Transmission.
How long an infected character has before the infection kills them. Never means the infection doesn't kill. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Mortality.
How long after death an infected body gets back up as a zombie. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Reanimate.
How smart zombies are, meaning whether they can open doors and windows. Random uses 'Zombie door opening percentage'. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Cognition.
When 'Zombie cognition' is on Random, the percentage of zombies that can open doors. Ignored for the other 'Zombie cognition' choices. In the settings file: ZombieLore.DoorOpeningPercentage.
How often zombies crawl under parked cars to reach you. In the settings file: ZombieLore.CrawlUnderVehicle.
How long zombies keep chasing after they lose sight or sound of you. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Memory.
How far zombies can see. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Sight.
How far zombies can hear. In the settings file: ZombieLore.Hearing.

On: zombies use the newer sight rules, where a car between a zombie and a player on foot blocks its view and some objects give cover to sneaking players. Off: the older rules, which weigh light, distance and movement differently. Traits, rain and fog count either way. In the settings file: ZombieLore.SpottedLogic.
On: wandering zombies that haven't noticed anyone can still bash doors and builds. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ThumpNoChasing.
On: zombies can damage and destroy things players have built. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ThumpOnConstruction.

When zombies are fully active: Both, Night or Day. Outside their active time they move as shamblers whatever 'Zombie speed' says, are a quarter as likely to spot players, and forget them quickly. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ActiveOnly.
On: zombies breaking windows can set off house alarms. In the settings file: ZombieLore.TriggerHouseAlarm.
On: a group of zombies attacking at once can drag a character down and kill them. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ZombiesDragDown.
On: crawlers next to you also count towards being dragged down. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ZombiesCrawlersDragDown.
On: zombies can lunge at you right after climbing a fence or window if you're standing too close. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ZombiesFenceLunge.
Multiplies how much protection zombies get from armour they're wearing. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ZombiesArmorFactor.
The most protection, as a percentage, worn armour can give a zombie. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ZombiesMaxDefense.
Percentage chance a zombie has a weapon stuck in it. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ChanceOfAttachedWeapon.
Multiplies the damage zombies take from falling. In the settings file: ZombieLore.ZombiesFallDamage.
Whether some bodies that look dead get up and attack: world zombies only, world and combat zombies, or never. In the settings file: ZombieLore.DisableFakeDead.
Clears zombies from where a new character spawns: the building and around it, the building, the room, or nowhere. In the settings file: ZombieLore.PlayerSpawnZombieRemoval.

EnumValues.1: Inside the building and around it

Description: How many zombies it takes to start damaging a tall fence. Once a fence starts bending, fewer are needed. Below 1, zombies don't bend tall fences. In the settings file: ZombieLore.FenceThumpersRequired.
How quickly zombies damage tall fences. In the settings file: ZombieLore.FenceDamageMultiplier.
On: loot doesn't respawn inside claimed safehouses. Only matters when 'Loot respawn (hours)' is above 0. In the settings file: SafehousePreventsLootRespawn.

Loot amount for food that can rot in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: FoodLootNew.

Loot amount for books, fliers and newspapers (not skill books) in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: LiteratureLootNew.

Loot amount for skill books in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: SkillBookLoot.

Loot amount for items that teach recipes in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: RecipeResourceLoot.

Loot amount for medicine, bandages and first aid tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MedicalLootNew.

Loot amount for camping and fishing gear in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: SurvivalGearsLootNew.

Loot amount for canned and dried food and drinks in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: CannedFoodLootNew.

Loot amount for melee weapons in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: WeaponLootNew.

Loot amount for guns and attachments in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: RangedWeaponLootNew.

Loot amount for ammo, boxes and magazines in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: AmmoLootNew.

Loot amount for car parts and their tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MechanicsLootNew.

How often items that don't fit any other loot category spawn in containers. None stops them spawning. Foraging in towns and along roads isn't tied to this: it follows Nature's Abundance. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: OtherLootNew.

Loot amount for clothing in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ClothingLootNew.

Loot amount for bags and cases in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ContainerLootNew.

Loot amount for keys, key rings and locks in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This also sets the chance zombies and cars carry keys. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: KeyLootNew.

Loot amount for VHS tapes and CDs in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MediaLootNew.

Loot amount for Spiffo items, plushies and keepsakes in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MementoLootNew.

Loot amount for cooking items in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: CookwareLootNew.

Loot amount for crafting and building materials in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MaterialLootNew.

Loot amount for seeds and farming tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: FarmingLootNew.

Loot amount for other tools in containers. 0 means none. The settings screen choices are 0.05 insanely rare, 0.2 extremely rare, 0.4 rare, 0.6 normal, 2 common and 3 abundant. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ToolLootNew.

Multiplies how many times each container's loot table is rolled. The game warns not to change this; high values can hurt performance. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: RollsMultiplier.
Item types, separated by commas, that never spawn as normal loot. Spaces are ignored. Foraging uses this list too. In the settings file: LootItemRemovalList.

DisplayName: Keep removed items out of stories
Description: On: items on the loot removal list, or in a loot category set to None, also stay out of the random story scenes placed around the world. Off: those scenes can still place them. In the settings file: RemoveStoryLoot.
On: weapons the game attaches to zombies skip any item on the loot removal list or in a loot category set to None. Clothing zombies wear isn't affected. In the settings file: RemoveZombieLoot.

Above 0, places with more zombies nearby get more loot, scaled by this number. 0 turns this off. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ZombiePopLootEffect.
The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Insanely Rare. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this. In the settings file: InsaneLootFactor.
The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Extremely Rare. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this. In the settings file: ExtremeLootFactor.
The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Rare. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this. In the settings file: RareLootFactor.
The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Normal. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this. In the settings file: NormalLootFactor.
The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Common. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this. In the settings file: CommonLootFactor.
The spawn multiplier for generators when 'Generators' is set to Abundant. Nothing else in Build 42.21 reads this. In the settings file: AbundantLootFactor.

Stops loot refilling in a town area if players have been there within this many in-game hours. 0 turns the check off, so areas refill on schedule even if players were just there. Only matters when 'Loot respawn (hours)' is above 0. In the settings file: SeenHoursPreventLootRespawn.

How often looted containers in towns refill, in in-game hours. Only containers that have been looted at least once refill, and 0 turns it off. It's off in every Build 42 preset; servers that use it often pick 168 to 720 hours (1 week to 1 month). In the settings file: HoursForLootRespawn.
Containers holding this many items or more don't refill. In the settings file: MaxItemsForLootRespawn.

DisplayName: No loot respawn in built areas
Description: On: once players build, barricade, hang sheets or place furniture somewhere, loot stops respawning across that whole map zone, not just in that building. In the settings file: ConstructionPreventsLootRespawn.

Item types, separated by commas, that are cleared from the ground once 'Ground item removal (hours)' have passed since they were dropped. They're cleared when that part of the map next loads. In the settings file: WorldItemRemovalList.
DefaultValue: Base.Hat, Base.Glasses, Base.Maggots, Base.Slug, Base.Slug2, Base.Snail, Base.Worm, Base.Dung_Mouse, Base.Dung_Rat

Description: How many in-game hours an item has to lie on the ground before the removal list clears it. It goes the next time that part of the map loads. In the settings file: HoursForWorldItemRemoval.

Off: items on the world item removal list are cleared from the ground once they've lain there long enough. On: the list becomes a keep list, and ground items that aren't on it are cleared instead. In the settings file: ItemRemovalListBlacklistToggle.

How often generators turn up, from none to abundant. This covers generators in containers and generators placed in sheds, garages and storage rooms the first time they're seen; in rural ones it also sets the chance of a random workstation. For container loot, this is the only setting that uses the six Loot Factor settings. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: GeneratorSpawning.
How often a found map has a dead survivor's notes on it. In the settings file: AnnotatedMapChance.

How many in-game hours before dead bodies rot away and disappear. 0 or -1 means bodies stay and don't grow maggots. Player bodies follow the server setting 'Remove player bodies too'. In the settings file: HoursForCorpseRemoval.
How many in-game days after food rots before it's removed from the map. -1 means never. In the settings file: DaysForRottenFoodRemoval.

DisplayName: Largest building that can be pre-looted
Description: Buildings with more rooms than this aren't pre-looted or trashed. Shops are the exception: they can still turn up already looted whatever their size. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MaximumLootedBuildingRooms.

Days before old blood splats are cleaned away, checked when that part of the map loads. 0 means they stay forever. This is the copy the game reads, not the server setting of the same name. In the settings file: BloodSplatLifespanDays.

The highest chance, in percent, that a building is already looted and trashed when it's first found. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MaximumLooted.

How many days it takes to reach the 'Highest pre-looted building chance'. Before that, the chance grows day by day. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: DaysUntilMaximumLooted.

Meant to multiply the already-looted chance for buildings outside towns, but the game drops the decimals first. Below 1, rural buildings get the lowest chance (1 percent) and lose no loot over time; from 1 to just under 2 nothing changes; 2 doubles both. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: RuralLooted.

The highest share of loot, in percent, that stops spawning as days pass. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: MaximumDiminishedLoot.

How many days it takes to reach the 'Most loot lost over time (%)' amount. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: DaysUntilMaximumDiminishedLoot.
How long one in-game day lasts in real time. 2 hour days are a common choice for Build 42. In the settings file: DayLength.
The year the world starts in, from 1993 up to 2092. Not shown in the game's settings screens. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: StartYear.
The month the world starts in. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: StartMonth.

DisplayName: Start day of the month (new world only)
Description: The day of the month the world starts on. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: StartDay.
The hour of the day the world starts at. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: StartTime.
Normal days and nights, endless day, or endless night. In the settings file: DayNightCycle.

How many days until nature fully takes over (grass, vines and trees). This is fixed when the world is created, because the world keeps its own erosion file. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: ErosionSpeed.
A custom number of days for nature to fully take over. 0 uses 'Nature regrowth speed'. -1 stops nature growing at all, and that works on a running world too. In the settings file: ErosionDays.

DisplayName: Months since the outbreak (new world only)
Description: How many months after the outbreak the world begins, from 0 to 12. This sets how overgrown the world is when it's created, and affects bodies and skeletons in areas when they're first loaded. It also counts towards 'Water shutoff day' and 'Power shutoff day', so at 1 month or more, a 14 day shutoff means water and power are already off when the world starts. It doesn't change the start date. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: TimeSinceApo.
How dark nights are, from pitch black to bright. In the settings file: NightDarkness.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: How long nights are, from always night to always day. Not shown in the game's settings screens. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: NightLength.
Normal weather, or weather locked to one state: no weather, endless rain, endless storm, endless snow or endless blizzard. In the settings file: ClimateCycle.
Normal fog, no fog, or endless fog. In the settings file: FogCycle.
Shifts how cold or hot the seasons are. Applied each time the world loads. In the settings file: Temperature.
How often it rains. In the settings file: Rain.
How many items players find when foraging. In the settings file: NatureAbundance.
Caps how thick fog can look on screen. In the settings file: MaxFogIntensity.
Caps how heavy rain looks on screen. In the settings file: MaxRainFxIntensity.
On: snow builds up on the ground. Off: snow still shows on plants and roofs. In the settings file: EnableSnowOnGround.
How common and heavy rat and other vermin infestations are. 0 means none. In the settings file: MaximumRatIndex.
How many days it takes for vermin to reach the 'Vermin level' you've set. In the settings file: DaysUntilMaximumRatIndex.
How many fish are in rivers and lakes. In the settings file: FishAbundance.

The chance that dirt by lakes is turned into clay when the world generates new ground. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ClayLakeChance.

The chance that dirt by rivers is turned into clay when the world generates new ground. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ClayRiverChance.

DisplayName: Water shutoff range (single player, new world only)
Description: A range for when tap water stops. Only the single player new game screen uses this, to roll a random day into 'Water shutoff day'. Servers read 'Water shutoff day' directly, and the Host screen hides this choice. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: WaterShut.

DisplayName: Power shutoff range (single player, new world only)
Description: A range for when the power grid shuts off. Only the single player new game screen uses this, to roll a random day into 'Power shutoff day'. Servers read 'Power shutoff day' directly, and the Host screen hides this choice. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: ElecShut.
How long house alarm batteries last after the power goes. Rolled for each alarmed building when the map's building data is set up. In the settings file: AlarmDecay.

The day tap water stops, counted from the outbreak, so 'Months since the outbreak' counts towards it. -1 turns the water off from the very start. For water that never stops in practice, use a very large number such as 100000. Utilities going off around 30 days is common. In the settings file: WaterShutModifier.

The day the power grid shuts off, counted from the outbreak, so 'Months since the outbreak' counts towards it. -1 means there's no grid power from the very start. For power that never shuts off in practice, use a very large number such as 100000. Utilities going off around 30 days is common. In the settings file: ElecShutModifier.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: 'Alarm battery life' is the one the game uses. Not shown in the game's settings screens. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: AlarmDecayModifier.
Multiplies how much fuel a generator burns each in-game hour. A generator burns more the more it's powering, and 0 means it burns no fuel. In the settings file: GeneratorFuelConsumption.
On: generators work outdoors, which lets them power things such as fuel pumps. In the settings file: AllowExteriorGenerator.
On: fuel pumps never run dry. This overrides the pump minimum, maximum and empty chance settings. In the settings file: FuelStationGasInfinite.
The lowest amount of fuel a pump starts with, from 0 (empty) to 1 (full). In the settings file: FuelStationGasMin.
The highest amount of fuel a pump starts with, from 0 (empty) to 1 (full). In the settings file: FuelStationGasMax.
The chance, in percent, that a fuel pump starts empty. In the settings file: FuelStationGasEmptyChance.
How long light bulbs last. Higher lasts longer, and 0 means bulbs never break. Car headlights aren't affected. In the settings file: LightBulbLifespan.
How far, in tiles, a generator sends power sideways. In the settings file: GeneratorTileRange.
How many floors above and below a generator get power. In the settings file: GeneratorVerticalPowerRange.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: The old farming speed choice, hidden from the game's settings screens. 'Farming speed', the number box, is the one used. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: Farming.
How long food takes to turn into compost, from 1 to 12 weeks. In the settings file: CompostTime.
How fast food spoils, in or out of a fridge. In the settings file: FoodRotSpeed.
How well fridges keep food fresh. No decay means chilled food never spoils. In the settings file: FridgeFactor.
How much water crops lose each day and how well they resist disease. In the settings file: PlantResilience.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: The old harvest size choice, hidden from the game's settings screens. Its replacement, 'Harvest size', doesn't change harvests in 42.21 either. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: PlantAbundance.
How fast animals get hungry and thirsty. In the settings file: AnimalStatsModifier.
How fast animals get hungry and thirsty while nobody's nearby. Not shown in the game's settings screens. In the settings file: AnimalMetaStatsModifier.
How long animal pregnancies last. In the settings file: AnimalPregnancyTime.
How fast animals age. Slow and Very Slow work the same as Normal. In the settings file: AnimalAgeModifier.
How fast animals build up milk. In the settings file: AnimalMilkIncModifier.
How fast animals grow wool. In the settings file: AnimalWoolIncModifier.
How often farms start with animals. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: AnimalRanchChance.
In-game hours for grass to grow back after animals eat it or it's cut. In the settings file: AnimalGrassRegrowTime.
On: an unseen predator may kill chickens or turkeys in a hutch if its door is left open at night. In the settings file: AnimalMetaPredator.
On: animals only breed and lay in their season. Off: all year. In the settings file: AnimalMatingSeason.
How long eggs take to hatch. In the settings file: AnimalEggHatch.
On: animal noises draw nearby zombies. In the settings file: AnimalSoundAttractZombies.
How often wild animals leave tracks. In the settings file: AnimalTrackChance.

How often animal paths for hunting are created when the world generates new areas. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: AnimalPathChance.
Whether players can add poison to food: True for yes, False for no, or yes except bleach. In the settings file: EnablePoisoning.
Where maggots can appear on corpses: in and around bodies, in bodies only, or never. In the settings file: MaggotSpawn.
On: crops and herbs grown indoors slowly lose health until they die. House plants, and crops in a greenhouse, aren't affected. In the settings file: KillInsideCrops.

On: seasons matter for crops. Players can sow any month, but crops sown outside their season start weaker, outdoor crops suffer in their bad months and in winter unless they're cold hardy, and sowing in a crop's best month can give a bonus harvest. Off: crops grow the same all year. In the settings file: PlantGrowingSeasons.
On: players can farm above the ground floor. The game warns this can hurt performance. In the settings file: PlaceDirtAboveground.
Multiplies how fast crops grow. In the settings file: FarmingSpeedNew.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: Meant to multiply how much a crop gives at harvest. In 42.21 the game works out the multiplied amount but then hands out the normal one, so this doesn't change harvests. In the settings file: FarmingAmountNew.
The most hours of fuel a campfire or stove can hold. In the settings file: MaximumFireFuelHours.
How fast hunger, thirst and tiredness build up. In the settings file: StatsDecrease.
On: new characters start with chips, a water bottle, a small backpack, a baseball bat and a hammer. In the settings file: StarterKit.
On: what characters eat affects their weight and health. In the settings file: Nutrition.
How fast characters get their breath back after effort. In the settings file: EndRegen.
Extra trait points at character creation. A negative number gives fewer. In the settings file: CharacterFreePoints.
On: every clothing item can be picked at character creation. In the settings file: AllClothesUnlocked.
How the media list shows media your players haven't seen yet: fully revealed, shown as ???, or completely hidden. In the settings file: MetaKnowledge.
On: players can see recipes at a crafting station before they've learnt them. In the settings file: SeeNotLearntRecipe.
From this skill level up, TV, VHS and other media stop giving XP for that skill. In the settings file: LevelForMediaXPCutoff.

From this skill level up, scrapping furniture stops giving XP for that skill, so 0 means scrapping gives no XP. Electrical isn't affected and always gives XP. In the settings file: LevelForDismantleXPCutoff.
How many in-game days before re-reading the same magazine or book helps again. In the settings file: LiteratureCooldown.
Whether picking many negative traits gives fewer bonus points. None means no penalty. In the settings file: NegativeTraitsPenalty.

EnumValues.2: 1 point penalty for every 3 negative traits selected
EnumValues.3: 1 point penalty for every 2 negative traits selected
EnumValues.4: 1 point penalty for every negative trait selected after the first

Description: How many in-game minutes it takes to read one page of a skill book. In the settings file: MinutesPerPage.

Multiplies muscle strain from swinging weapons and tools, firing guns and carrying heavy loads. 0 turns that strain off, but some crafting actions still cause strain whatever this is set to. In the settings file: MuscleStrainFactor.
Multiplies discomfort from worn clothing. 0 turns clothing discomfort off. Worn bags aren't affected by this. In the settings file: DiscomfortFactor.
On: randomly tinted clothes skip the darkest, near black shades. In the settings file: NoBlackClothes.
On: climbing sheet ropes and walls never fails. In the settings file: EasyClimbing.
Multiplies XP for every skill, but only while the global multiplier is switched on. 1.5 to 2 is common; public listings advertise 2 to 3. In the settings file: MultiplierConfig.Global.
On: the global XP multiplier applies to every skill and the per-skill multipliers are ignored. Off: each skill uses its own multiplier. In the settings file: MultiplierConfig.GlobalToggle.
Multiplies XP for the Fitness skill. Only used when the global multiplier is switched off. In the settings file: MultiplierConfig.Fitness.

How many bonus hit points player-built things get on top of their base hit points, so they last longer against zombies. Normal gives the usual bonus, Very Low halves it and Very High adds half again. It's set when each thing is built. In the settings file: ConstructionBonusPoints.
On: characters can break bones from falls, being hit by a car and car crashes. In the settings file: BoneFracture.
How bad injuries are and how long they take to heal. In the settings file: InjurySeverity.
How much rotting bodies nearby make a character sick. Sickness only starts with more than 5 bodies nearby. None turns this off. In the settings file: DecayingCorpseHealthImpact.
On: living zombies nearby count like rotting bodies, so they can make a character sick too. This does nothing when 'Rotting bodies affect health' is None. In the settings file: ZombieHealthImpact.
How much blood sprays onto floors and walls, from None to Ultra Gore. In the settings file: BloodLevel.

How much blood and dirt clothes pick up, and how dirty, bloody and torn zombies' clothes are when they spawn. This doesn't change how fast clothes lose condition. In 42.21, Fast adds less blood and dirt to clothes than Normal does. In the settings file: ClothingDegradation.
On: fire spreads to nearby things. In the settings file: FireSpread.
On: some attack and body dragging animations slow you down while they play. In the settings file: AttackBlockMovements.

On: tainted water and tainted food are labelled as tainted, and automatic drinking skips tainted water. Off: tainted water isn't labelled, and automatic drinking can pick it. In the settings file: EnableTaintedWaterText.
On: some melee weapons can hit several zombies in one swing. In the settings file: MultiHitZombies.
How likely a zombie attacking from behind or the side is to injure or bite. High is the most dangerous. In the settings file: RearVulnerability.
Lets infected wounds hurt a character who's already at the worst level of sickness. 0 turns this damage off, and higher values make it kick in sooner. In the settings file: WoundInfectionFactor.

What happens when a gunshot fails its hit roll. Disabled: it misses. Zombies only: a zombie is still hit but takes no damage, and other targets are missed. All types of target: any target is still hit but takes no damage. In the settings file: FirearmUseDamageChance.
Multiplies how far away zombies can hear gunshots. In the settings file: FirearmNoiseMultiplier.
Multiplies the chance guns jam. 0 means guns never jam. In the settings file: FirearmJamMultiplier.
Multiplies how much moodles (panic, tiredness and so on) hurt aim. 0 turns that off. In the settings file: FirearmMoodleMultiplier.
Multiplies how much wind, rain and fog hurt aim. 0 turns that off. In the settings file: FirearmWeatherMultiplier.
On: headgear such as welding masks affects aim. In the settings file: FirearmHeadGearEffect.
On: players can open a mini-map. This only works when 'World map allowed' is on. In the settings file: Map.AllowMiniMap.
On: players can open the full world map. In the settings file: Map.AllowWorldMap.
On: the world map starts fully revealed. In the settings file: Map.MapAllKnown.

On: players can't open the world map when it's too dark to read, unless they're holding or wearing a light or sitting in a car with a working battery. Admins aren't affected. Paper maps need light whatever this is set to. In the settings file: Map.MapNeedsLight.
How likely a house is to have an alarm. This is rolled for buildings when the map's building data is set up. In the settings file: Alarm.

How often house doors and windows are locked. Each door or window is set when it's first created from the map. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: LockedHouses.

How often the helicopter event flies over. The first flyover is picked for 6 to 9 nights in when the world starts and saved with the world, so switching to Never later doesn't cancel it. After that, Sometimes repeats every 10 to 15 days and Often every 6 to 9. In the settings file: Helicopter.
How often far-off events like gunshots happen, drawing zombies. In the settings file: MetaEvent.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: Meant to control zombie break-ins while a character sleeps, but in 42.21 the game never switches the break-in check on, so this has no effect. Nightmares happen whatever this is set to. In the settings file: SleepingEvent.

How often buildings get a story set-up, such as burnt out, a stash or bodies. This is rolled the first time a building is loaded. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: SurvivorHouseChance.
How often road stories appear, such as police roadblocks. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: VehicleStoryChance.
How often scene stories appear in map zones, such as a forest campsite. This only affects places nobody has visited yet. Explored areas keep what they had. In the settings file: ZoneStoryChance.

Subcategory: Not used by the game in 42.21:block:99
Description: Shown in the game's settings screens as how often basements appear. The game (version 42.21) doesn't use this setting, so changing it does nothing. In the settings file: Basement.SpawnFrequency.
